minors.why: Purely cosmetic — Prettier does not reflow comments, so lint stays green and it will survive indefinitely. This docblock is the one place a future maintainer will read to understand why neither half of the module uses fflate's async API; a visibly half-edited paragraph invites the next reader to distrust the rest of it.

verification.test: pnpm test (vitest run) — exit 0, 184 passed (8 files), matching the stated baseline. Re-run at the end of the review after all revert-and-restore work: still 184/184, and src/main/document/store.ts hashes identically to the pristine copy taken before any edit (md5 aaecc9aad14e606fa721646a3c03e6ea).
verification.environment: node v24.18.1, pnpm. All scratch probes were written to a temporary tests/unit/document/zz-probe.test.ts and deleted; `jj diff --summary -r @` at the end lists exactly the 24 paths it listed at the start.

hypotheses_tested: H1 (r5 B1 — is the async-zip write-path fan-out actually gone, and is the fix revert-proof?): REJECTED as a defect. packDeck now ends in `zipSync(zippable as Zippable, { level: 6 })` (store.ts:1085); the only fflate imports are Inflate/strFromU8/strToU8/zipSync (store.ts:100), so neither `zip` nor `unzip` is reachable from src/. Revert test: swapping zipSync back for a promisified async `zip` reds exactly one test — store.test.ts:1306 'deflates on the calling thread — no event-loop turn, so no worker fan-out' (1 failed / 167 passed). The probe is structural rather than an RSS measurement: async zip cannot deliver without a macrotask turn, zipSync returns before an already-queued setImmediate runs. The docblock (store.ts:11-23) and the tech-stack row (.claude/plans/init/11-tech-stack.md:38) now both attribute the fan-out to fflate's asynchronous API in **both** directions, which was r5's documentation complaint.

H2 (r5 major 1 — silent under-delivery): REJECTED as a defect. `if (produced !== allowed) throw new ZipExtractError(...)` is present at store.ts:624-628. Revert test: deleting that block reds exactly one test — store.test.ts:1272 'rejects a DEFLATE member that delivers fewer bytes than it declared', which crafts the r5 PoC directly (zeroes compressedSize in both the central header at +20 and the local header at +18, so the two still agree) and asserts code 'not-a-zip' with message 'produced 0 bytes but declared'. 1 failed / 167 passed.

H3 (r5 major 2a/2b — local-vs-central name and method checks): REJECTED as a defect. Reverting the name check (store.ts:565-567) to a no-op reds exactly one test, store.test.ts:1244 (1 failed / 167 passed). Reverting the method check (store.ts:568-570) reds exactly one test, store.test.ts:1259 (1 failed / 167 passed). Both tests craft real header corruption on a packed fixture via craftHeaders/centralDirectory (store.test.ts:1202-1234) rather than mocking, so they pin behaviour, not implementation.

H4 (r5 major 2c — the racing deadline timer): REJECTED as a defect. Replacing the timer arm of the Promise.race (store.ts:849-857) with `new Promise<never>(() => undefined)` reds exactly one test — tests/unit/document/store-extraction-deadline.test.ts:42 (1 failed / 167 passed). The test is honest about what it injects: `vi.mock('node:timers', () => ({ setImmediate: () => undefined }))` swallows the between-members yield, which is a hang *inside* the extraction promise — precisely the state the in-loop `Date.now() > deadline` checks can never reach, so the timer is the sole thing that can settle it. store.ts imports setImmediate from node:timers (line 99) specifically so this is mockable, and `setTimeout` is taken from the global, so the mock cannot accidentally disable the timer it is testing. The mock is module-wide, which is why it correctly lives in its own file.

H5 (r5 minor 1 — 'extraction-timeout' code and its mapping order): REJECTED as a defect, and the ordering is itself pinned. `ZipTimeoutError extends ZipExtractError` (store.ts:535), so catch order is load-bearing: store.ts:860-863 tests ZipTooLargeError, then ZipTimeoutError, then falls through to 'not-a-zip'. Revert test: deleting only the ZipTimeoutError branch reds two tests (store.test.ts:1092 'always settles' and the deadline file), 2 failed / 166 passed — so both the in-loop timeout path (extractionTimeoutMs: -1) and the racing-timer path are asserted to produce code 'extraction-timeout' rather than 'not-a-zip'.

H6 (r5 minors 2 and 3 — stale comment and the O(1) claim): REJECTED as defects. The redundant null-prototype re-key loop is gone: store.ts:871 is now `const entries = raw` with a comment explaining that extractMembers already returns an emptyMap. The peak-allocation docblock (store.ts:586-590) now states the real constant, '`allowed` plus at most ~2 MB of transient push output'. I re-derived the bound from the code rather than accepting it: the overshoot a single push can hide is bounded by the feed sizing at store.ts:613-614 — when the remaining allowance drops under ~1.05 MB the feed is clamped to MIN_FEED_BYTES (1024), so at most 1024 * 1032 ≈ 1.06 MB can land before the overflow check runs, doubled by fflate's internal buffer growth. Above that the headroom formula keeps feed * 1032 at or under the remaining allowance, so the 16 kB MAX_FEED_BYTES ceiling never produces a larger transient. The stated ~2 MB is correct.

H7 (NEW — does the new `produced !== allowed` check false-positive on archives from a third-party zipper?): REJECTED. This was my main worry about the r5 major-1 fix: a strict equality against the declared inflated size will reject any real-world archive whose writer is sloppy about that field, and the degenerate cases (zero-length and 1-byte members, where DEFLATE expands rather than compresses) are exactly where writers differ. Built a .sloodge with python3's `zipfile` at ZIP_DEFLATED containing the full fixture deck plus `assets/empty.bin` (zero bytes) and `assets/tiny.bin` (one byte). readDeck returns ok:true. So the check is exact for DEFLATE as the docblock claims, and the STORED branch never reaches it.

H8 (NEW — collisions with the two entries packDeck writes before `claim` runs): REJECTED. `zippable[MIMETYPE_ENTRY]` and `zippable[MANIFEST_ENTRY]` are assigned directly (store.ts:1010-1011), bypassing `claim`, so an extras entry named `mimetype` or `manifest.json` meets an already-occupied slot. Verified through the shipped API: extras['mimetype'] with different bytes rejects with 'two different payloads claim the archive entry mimetype'; with byte-identical content it is a silent no-op and — the part that matters for OPC — `mimetype` is still the first entry in the written archive, still STORED. The `existing instanceof Uint8Array ? existing : existing?.[0]` unwrap at store.ts:1024 handles the `[bytes, {level:0}]` tuple form correctly.

H9 (NEW — is the synchronous write a main-process freeze at the shipped caps?): REJECTED. The module docblock defends the sync stall as 'a bounded stall is recoverable, an OOM kill is not', which is only a fair trade if the stall is actually small; the write path, unlike the read path, has no deadline and never yields. Measured zipSync at level 6 on this machine: 16 MB → 134 ms, 64 MB → 480 ms, 200 MB → 1447 ms, and 64 MB of pseudo-random (incompressible) data → 554 ms. So even a deck at the 256 MB `maxTotalBytes` ceiling is ~2 s, not the tens of seconds that would make this a UI defect, and a real deck is milliseconds. Not worth a finding; the signature is already a Promise so the worker-thread move stays available.

H10 (NEW — degenerate deck shapes through the real API): REJECTED. A zero-slide deck (`createEmptyDeck` with empty slides/slideOrder) writeDecks and readDecks back cleanly — the schema allows it and the `wanted.length === 0` short-circuit at store.ts:846 is not reachable for it (mimetype and manifest.json are still members), so both branches of that race exist for real inputs. readDeck on a *directory* path returns an error value rather than throwing (the stat succeeds, the readFile EISDIR is caught at store.ts:730-733 and mapped to 'io'). No path pollutes Object.prototype.

H11 (NEW — ZIP64 extra-field arithmetic and loop termination in the code r5 did not re-derive): REJECTED. `resolveZip64Sizes` (store.ts:351-385) advances by `4 + size` per field, so a zero-length field still advances 4 and the `offset + 4 <= end` loop always terminates. The consume order (uncompressed 8 bytes first if 0xffffffff, then compressed) matches APPNOTE 4.5.3, including the asymmetric case where only compressedSize is 0xffffffff. The ZIP64 EOCD bounds guard checks `zip64Eocd + 56 > bytes.length` before reading getBigUint64 at +32 and +48 (max byte 55), so it cannot read out of range. A ZIP64 local-header offset stored as 0xffffffff is *not* resolved into `localHeaderOffset` (store.ts:510 reads it as a bare u32) — but that lands in `memberDataRange`'s `need()` as an out-of-range offset and surfaces as 'not-a-zip', and a >4 GB archive is refused by `maxCompressedBytes` long before, so it is a correct outcome rather than a gap.

H12 (repo conventions, trust boundaries, dependency policy): REJECTED. `src/shared/document/**` imports only zod and its siblings (`../slide-id`, which exists and predates this change); `src/main/document/store.ts` imports only node builtins, fflate and `src/shared`; nothing imports electron, React, or across a forbidden direction, and oxlint's no-restricted-imports overrides are green. The single `oxlint-disable-next-line` in the changeset (store.ts:694) suppresses `no-await-in-loop` on the sequential-yield await, which is the entire point of that loop, not a dependency-direction rule. Both trust boundaries — manifest JSON and theme JSON out of an untrusted archive — go through zod `safeParse` behind a `findProtoKey` pre-scan; there is no cast at either. No IPC channel, no webPreferences, no iframe sandbox attribute is touched by this changeset. `fflate` and `zod` are both `catalog:` in package.json with matching pnpm-workspace.yaml entries, both pure JS (no native modules), and fflate now has a justifying row in .claude/plans/init/11-tech-stack.md that names the fan-out hazard and the mitigation. All new logic is Electron-free and reachable from Vitest — 184 tests, none requiring an Electron host.

notes.summary: All six r5 findings are genuinely fixed, and — the part r5 asked for and did not have — each fix is now individually revert-proof: I reverted the zipSync write path, the under-delivery check, the local-header name check, the local-header method check, the racing deadline timer, and the 'extraction-timeout' mapping one at a time, and each revert turned red exactly the guard test written for it (the mapping revert reds two, its in-loop and its racing-timer path), with the tree restored byte-identically afterwards. The new code this round added holds up under fresh attack: the strict `produced !== allowed` equality does not false-positive on a python-zipfile DEFLATE archive containing zero-length and 1-byte members, the deadline test's node:timers mock injects a hang the in-loop checks provably cannot see (so it tests the timer and nothing else), packDeck's pre-zipSync entry/byte bounds sit ahead of the allocation and its two directly-assigned entries still collide safely through `claim`, and the synchronous write is ~1.4 s at the 200 MB mark rather than the freeze the sync trade would have to justify. lint, typecheck and test are green from my own run at 184/184. Ship it; the only thing left is a half-edited paragraph in the module docblock.
